sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 641 of 2018
Revisionist :- Suprabhat Banerjee

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Anr.
Counsel for Revisionist :- Mohd.Saulat Wasim,Jyoti Rajpoot,Ranjit Yadav,Sachida Nand,Sal
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate,Sanjay Kumar Srivastava,Vivek Kumar Tripath
Hon'ble Subhash Vidyarthi,J.
1.

Heard Sri Ranjit Yadav, the learned counsel for the revisionist, Sri Puneet Kumar Yadav, the learned State Counsel, Sri Shivesh Nath Dubey, holding brief of Sri B.D. Sharma, the learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 and perused the record.

2. The revisionist had filed the instant revision against an order dated 30.06.2018 passed by the Additional District and Sessions Judge, Court No. 12, Lucknow dismissing Criminal Appeal No. 38 of 2018, which was filed by the applicant against the judgment and order dated 19.01.2018 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 32, Lucknow in Criminal Case No. 5847 of 2014, arising out of Case Crime No. 57 of 2013, under Sections 498A, 323, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Bazar Khala, District Lucknow.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Court No. 12, Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 32, Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. By means of the impugned order, the trial court had convicted the applicant for offences under Section 498-A IPC and Section 4 of the D.P. Act and had sentenced him to undergo imprisonment for two years and pay Rs. 5,000/- as fine under Section 498-A and to undergo imprisonment for six months and pay fine of Rs. 2,000/-for the offences under Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
Suprabhat Banerjee vs State Of U.P. And Anr. on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85127327/
1 4. During pendency of this revision, the parties have entered into a compromise, which has been brought on record along with a supplementary affidavit and it is stated in the compromise that the complainant-opposite party no. 2 has resolved all her disputes with the revisionist and she does not want continuance of any proceedings against the revisionist.
5. The learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 has accepted the factum of compromise and supported the prayer for decision of the case in terms of the compromise between the parties.
6. The learned AGA has submitted that the State has conducted the prosecution right from initiation of the case by lodging of the FIR till this date during pendency of revision filed against conviction order, which has been affirmed by the appellate court and, therefore, although he has no objection against the proceedings being quashed on the ground of compromise between the parties, fine that was imposed on the revisionist by means of impugned order passed by the trial court, should be ordered to be paid to the State as cost of litigation from the trial court up to this Court.
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Section 357 Cr.P.C. contains a provision for imposition of fine and for utilization of the amount of fine in payment of cost of litigation incurred by the prosecution.
8. Accordingly, the revision is allowed in terms of the compromise.
The conviction and sentence of the revisionist imposed by the impugned order dated dated 19.01.2018 passed by the trial court is hereby set aside.
The learned counsel for the revisionist stated that the revisionist has already deposited the amount of fine before the trial court.

As the revisionist stands acquitted on the basis of compromise, it is provided that the amount deposited in the trial court shall be treated as cost of litigation incurred by the prosecution and shell be forwarded by the trial court to the U.P. State Legal Services Authority.

Order Date :- 15.3.2024 Pradeep/-
